<!-- go-guitar-pro-capability-work:lyrics -->

Project ordered Song.Lyrics lines onto their selected GPIF track without merging unrelated lyric scopes or mutating the input song.

**Type:** implementation. **Priority:** P2. **Capability:** `lyrics`.
**Formats:** gp3, gp4, gp5, gp6, gp7, gp8. **Stages to assess:** export.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For a valid TrackIndex and a track without lyrics, export the exact ordered legacy lines and starting-measure offsets; verify the index-base conversion with a real legacy fixture.
- [ ] If existing Track.Lyrics are equivalent, emit one copy. If they conflict, keep explicit track lyrics authoritative and report the omitted conflicting score lyrics; strict policy must reject an unallowed conflict.
- [ ] Retain empty/Unicode text and nonzero offsets with exact wire and Go reparse evidence; use pinned AlphaTab for supported lyric text/dispatch behavior.
- [ ] Unassigned legacy lyrics remain an explicit loss and invalid track references remain diagnosed. Keep beat lyrics and Beat.Text independent; remove only the resolved blanket score-lyrics omission.

Any public API change must expose the authored value with a documented edit/reconciliation contract. Add a non-default public API regression and independent pinned-consumer export evidence. Preserve compatibility or explicitly document the change.

## Scope boundaries

- Do not concatenate conflicting representations or silently assign unassigned lyrics to track zero.

## Reproduction and evidence

For a valid TrackIndex and a track without lyrics, export the exact ordered legacy lines and starting-measure offsets; verify the index-base conversion with a real legacy fixture. See the linked investigation decision and review receipt for the confirmed baseline.

Use the named fixtures and non-default cases above. The linked investigation and review distinguish reproduced failures from source-backed implementation gaps.

- AlphaTab [Beat.lyrics](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/blob/022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d/packages/alphatab/src/model/Beat.ts#L388)
- AlphaTab [Lyrics.startBar](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/blob/022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d/packages/alphatab/src/model/Lyrics.ts#L28)
- AlphaTab [Lyrics.text](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/blob/022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d/packages/alphatab/src/model/Lyrics.ts#L34)
- AlphaTab [Lyrics.chunks](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/blob/022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d/packages/alphatab/src/model/Lyrics.ts#L39)
- Repository [gpif_parser.go](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/30436b08bf7f342ceda0d97c5ddd2c085db1b4f1/gpif_parser.go)
- Repository [gp8_builder.go](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/30436b08bf7f342ceda0d97c5ddd2c085db1b4f1/gp8_builder.go)
- field: `Song.Lyrics`. Public contract; linked matrix cases are in obligation.
- field: `Track.Lyrics`. Public contract; linked matrix cases are in obligation.
- investigation-review: `https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/issues/98#issuecomment-5624498716`. implementation-ready: The legacy selected-track lines have a GPIF Track.Lyrics destination already supported by both parsers; export currently omits Song.Lyrics unconditionally.

Oracle: AlphaTab 1.8.4, revision `022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d`. Audit baseline: `30436b08bf7f342ceda0d97c5ddd2c085db1b4f1`.

## Dependencies and coordination

No hard prerequisite.

Before claiming, refresh issue state and check `ready_work` and `work_conflicts`. Mark the work item `in_progress` with an owner. Source pointers are starting points; shared-file overlap is advisory and not an exhaustive conflict map.

## Investigation complete — implementation-ready

**Disposition: implement score-level lyric projection onto the selected GPIF track.**

Legacy GP lyrics store one selected TrackIndex plus five ordered lines of StartMeasureIndex/Text. The pinned GP3–5 importer reads that structure and applies the lines to the selected track. GPIF represents the same semantic as per-track Lyrics lines with Offset/Text, which pinned AlphaTab parses/writes and Go already supports as 'Track.Lyrics'.

**Next-step contract:** when 'Song.Lyrics.TrackIndex' is valid, project its ordered lines into that target track. If the track has no lyrics, copy them; if the two representations are identical, deduplicate; if they conflict, retain a deterministic authority rule and emit an explicit loss/conflict report instead of concatenating. Keep invalid/unassigned TrackIndex as a target limit. Beat-attached lyrics are a separate GPIF feature and must not be merged into these track lines. Test exact offsets/text, line order, Go reparse, and pinned AlphaTab.

Reviewed: legacy lyrics reader, GPIF lyrics paths, [pinned AlphaTab](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/tree/022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d). <!-- investigation-decision-ready-2026-09-10 -->

<!-- go-guitar-pro-capability-work:metadata -->

Fix GP8 metadata text serialization that silently corrupts line breaks in the pinned consumer, and complete independent coverage for supported credits/notices while retaining explicit legacy-only metadata omissions.

**Type:** implementation. **Priority:** P2. **Capability:** `metadata`.
**Formats:** gp3, gp4, gp5, gp6, gp7, gp8. **Stages to assess:** export.

**Current direction:** Fix independently proven metadata text cases and add raw consumer regressions. One CDATA retains boundary whitespace; ordinary escaped text retains a literal CDATA terminator without boundary whitespace. Their combination needs an independently verified encoding or a precise strict consumer-loss policy: pinned AlphaTab retains only the final CDATA section and trims ordinary text boundaries. Retain existing legacy-only omissions and notice slice-boundary reports.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A valid score with Notice=["First notice","Second notice"] must export under strict preservation with no loss report and raw pinned AlphaTab notices equal "First notice\nSecond notice". The current output yields a NUL separator and is a failing regression.
- [ ] Preserve supported metadata text with embedded line breaks, tabs, XML metacharacters and Unicode. Independently cover boundary whitespace without a CDATA terminator and a literal CDATA terminator without boundary whitespace; retaining encodings are verified for both classes. Assert raw consumer Music, Tabber, Instructions and Notices independently; Author and Transcriber must not alias Writer or each other.
- [ ] For boundary whitespace combined with the literal CDATA terminator, require a verified retaining encoding or a precise consumer-loss report and strict refusal with zero bytes. Test the exact string LF + TAB + A<&]]>B + TAB + LF. Preserve the full XML/Go text; do not accept the suffix-only result from split CDATA. An unrelated allowance must not bypass the new loss. Record the exact remaining consumer normalization when explicitly allowed.
- [ ] For notices ["", "embedded\nline", ""], permissive/allowlisted output must retain the joined target string "\nembedded\nline\n" exactly in the raw consumer; Go import may split the embedded line and must retain the existing gp8.normalize.notice-lines report. Separately test one empty notice with gp8.omit.empty-notice and ordinary leading/trailing empty entries that are representable as separators.
- [ ] Retain exact gp8.omit.writer/comments/date/clipboard-range reports for independent nondefault values. Strict export rejects unallowed losses and selective allowlisting cannot hide a remaining metadata loss.
- [ ] Fix encoding without repurposing credits or adding undocumented target fields; keep capability export partial because binary-only fields and notice slice-boundary limits remain.

For semantic changes, expose authored values with a documented edit/reconciliation contract and add non-default public API regressions with independent pinned-consumer export evidence. For inventory-only changes, verify the exact classification and its evidence without adding an unsupported API. Preserve compatibility or explicitly document the change.

## Scope boundaries

- No attempt to preserve distinct legacy Writer/Comments/Date/clipboard values in unrelated GPIF fields.
- No oracle upgrade or broad normalization of NUL/whitespace differences.

## Reproduction and evidence

At baseline, semanticValidPitchedGP8Song with notation=true and Notice=["First notice","Second notice"] produces11478 bytes and zero reports with RequirePreservation=true. Extract Content/score.gpif: Notices contains 
. Load the archive through pinned ScoreLoader and inspect score.notices directly: separator is U+0000. Existing normalized metadata projection omits notices and tab. A temp archive experiment replacing Notices with CDATA preserved exact leading/trailing line breaks; decimal entities repaired interior line breaks but were trimmed at boundaries. Choose any target-valid encoding proven by the raw consumer, including safe handling of a CDATA terminator. For the embedded temporary Go harness, first run mkdir -p /tmp/investigation-conversion; use t.TempDir when converting it to permanent tests. The raw consumer command below runs from the repository root after conformance dependencies are installed; replace /absolute/path/to/output.gp with the exported archive.

Use the source review and reproductions below as starting evidence. Add the fixture or inventory regression specified by the acceptance criteria; the lack of a saved probe is not evidence of support.

- AlphaTab [Score.album](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/blob/022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d/packages/alphatab/src/model/Score.ts#L243). 
- AlphaTab [Score.artist](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/blob/022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d/packages/alphatab/src/model/Score.ts#L248).

- review-next-steps: `https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/issues/99#issuecomment-5625490016`. - Repository [gp8_export.go:91](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/8d729442b6d2a7f56d304e34b279c143a15ddf1f/gp8_export.go#L91). encoding/xml.MarshalIndent emits hexadecimal numeric entities for line breaks.

For leading/trailing empty entries and an embedded line break, each exported hexadecimal newline entity also becomes U+0000. Decimal entities retain the interior LF but the consumer trims boundary LFs. A CDATA candidate retains the exact leading, interior and trailing LFs. ## Investigation complete — target limit

**Disposition: confirmed binary-only metadata limits; retain explicit omissions.**

The pinned GPIF Score record supports Title, Subtitle, Artist, Album, Words, Music, WordsAndMusic fallback, Copyright, Tabber, Instructions, and Notices. It has no distinct Writer, Comments, Date, or clipboard provenance/range fields. Repurposing Music, Tabber, or Notices would corrupt supported metadata, so the current omission reports are correct.

GPIF Notices is one newline-separated string. Consequently a public slice cannot preserve every boundary: embedded newlines, an empty notice, and multiple notices can collapse to the same target string. Keep the current notices normalization report and strict behavior. Author continues to map to Music independently; Writer must not alias it. No implementation follow-up is justified without an actual GP7/GP8 field and consumer evidence.

Reviewed: GPIF Score parser/writer and 'gp8_builder.go'. <!-- investigation-decision-ready-2026-09-10 -->

<!-- capability-review-next-steps-2026-09-10 -->

## Next steps after review

1. Exercise distinct Writer, Comments, Date and clipboard values plus ambiguous notice boundaries, including embedded newlines and empty entries. Assert current omission/normalization codes and strict behavior.

2. Cross-check the supported GPIF Score fields so Author/Music, Tabber, Instructions and Notices remain independent; do not repurpose one to hide unsupported metadata.

3. If the acceptance cases already pass, record their verified commit and resolve as narrow target limits. A future implementation needs an actual distinct target field and retaining consumer evidence.

Before closing, check every acceptance criterion against the exact verified commit and record the decision/evidence in the canonical work item and SQLite inventory. Issue closure alone must not promote support.

<!-- capability-actionability-review-2026-09-11 -->

Converted this investigation to a bounded implementation ticket.

This now has concrete production work: the pinned XML reader corrupts Go-emitted hex line-break entities while strict export reports success. A retaining encoding exists (CDATA was independently proved). Fix supported metadata text and add raw consumer checks; preserve the previously identified legacy omissions and notice-boundary reports.

The body now records the exact inputs, missing assertions, scope boundaries, source references and acceptance checklist.
